newsitem.title: USA: California governor vetoes welfare plan.
newsitem.headline: California governor vetoes welfare plan.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Monday delivered a blow to Democrats in the state legislature, vetoing their welfare reform plan even before lawmakers could finished voting on the package.
The state Senate and Assembly, both controlled by Democrats, approved three out of the four bills in the welfare package. Only one Republican lawmaker broke ranks to support the Democratic plan.
But before the Assembly could complete its voting on the final bill, Wilson, a Republican, vetoed a major component of the welfare package.

"The policies embodied in these bills not only perpetuate a gravely flawed system that discourages work, encourages dependency and inhibits a county's ability to design a system specific to the needs of their community and neediest citizens, they make it worse. Much worse," Wilson said in his veto message.

Republicans contend that the Democratic plan would be too generous and far too expensive. Wilson's office said the Democratic package would cost the state $1 billion more each year than the governor's own welfare proposal.
Wilson and legislative leaders planned to meet Monday night to discuss the welfare bills in hope of reaching a compromise in the coming days.
Welfare reform has been a major stumbling block for lawmakers negotiating California's budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year, which began July 1. The state's Constitutional budget deadline was June 15.
